title: The Un-Drunk One's Thirst
en:
may the higher knowledge come from tasting the nectar of your devotion —
that state, lord, turn toward me,
keen as the not-yet-drunk one's thirst for the first drink.
brief: The poem does not shame longing.
logic: The poem does not shame longing. It asks that devotion, rather than possession, become the taste of longing
howto: When: When wanting something begins to feel like being incomplete. Act (suggested modern devotional adaptation): Read the whole petition once; let the desire be addressed to Śiva, without pretending its ordinary object has vanished. Return: Do the next honest thing about the desire; pursue or decline it without making the outcome a spiritual verdict.
how: When longing is loud: say the verse and let the object of the longing become the taste of devotion rather than the thing you'd grab.
feel: keep the ache — it is the rasa before it arrives; the thirst IS the practice.
sign: Return: Do the next honest thing about the desire; pursue or decline it without making the outcome a spiritual verdict.

title: The Wine of Non-Difference
en:
let me not spend one moment here as anything
other than your servant's vessel — one who reverently,
unceasingly drinks the rasa-wine of your non-difference.
brief: In the poem, separation becomes a longing for a beloved who is also the ground of experience.
logic: In the poem, separation becomes a longing for a beloved who is also the ground of experience. The longing remains intelligible; metaphysical unity is its contemplative horizon
howto: When: When you miss closeness or fear that devotion has gone cold. Act (suggested modern devotional adaptation): Read the complete image of drinking; picture a cup only if that image helps you attend. Return: Send the message, hold the boundary, or simply carry on without testing whether you feel united.
how: When you crave closeness to something: say it and re-cast — the wine is already poured (non-difference); you are the cup.
feel: warmth as if from a sip; the distance you wanted to close was the fiction.
sign: Return: Send the message, hold the boundary, or simply carry on without testing whether you feel united.

title: What Delight, Beloved
iast: ambudaiḥ śikhigaṇo vinādyate kā ratiḥ priya mayā vinādya te
en:
by clouds the peacock-flock is sounded —
what delight, beloved, without me today?
brief: The landscape can carry longing without making every cry your private catastrophe.
logic: The landscape can carry longing without making every cry your private catastrophe. This is aesthetic evocation; a Śaiva devotional adaptation is editorial, not the poem's proven genre
howto: When: When the absence of somebody is most audible. Act (suggested modern devotional adaptation): Read the complete couplet; notice how rain and the peacock make absence articulate. Return: Return to the real person or the weather; neither must answer you.
how: When longing for someone or something: say it as the peacock line — the cry is appropriate, beautiful, and will end with the rain. Feel the ache as weather: you are the bird, not the drowning.
sign: Return: Return to the real person or the weather; neither must answer you.
feel: FULL; no mantra claim

title: The Moon That Carries the Nectar
en:
give me one glance of yours — light, cool, pure,
like the moon's crescent, carrying nectar —
o lord, for my desire itself.
brief: The devotee does not command desire to disappear; the beloved is asked to illuminate it with tenderness.
logic: The devotee does not command desire to disappear; the beloved is asked to illuminate it with tenderness
howto: When: When desire has become urgent and impatient. Act (suggested modern devotional adaptation): Read the request for a glance once; if useful, recall moonlight rather than force an internal sensation. Return: Respond to the actual need calmly; desire may remain.
how: When desire runs hot: one breath in, offer the heat upward as the thing that needs the glance, and picture the crescent-cool gaze landing on it. The prayer cools by image, not by prohibition.
feel: the heat stays but stops being an emergency.
sign: Return: Respond to the actual need calmly; desire may remain.

title: Laughing, Dancing, Eating It All
en:
where he laughs and dances, where desire and hatred themselves are eaten,
where the nectar-rasa of devotion is drunk —
may i attain that state.
brief: The surprise is not that anger is fake; the poem pictures a freedom expansive enough not to be monopolised by aversion.
logic: The surprise is not that anger is fake; the poem pictures a freedom expansive enough not to be monopolised by aversion
howto: When: When something serious has become absurd in retrospect. Act (suggested modern devotional adaptation): Read the whole verse with its contrast between devotion and what is consumed or overcome. Return: Laugh if laughter comes; otherwise continue without forcing cheer.
how: Say it when something finally stops being infuriating — and notice the laugh that arrives is the verse working.
feel: the annoyance is suddenly chewable; that is bhujyate happening. Let the laugh be the proof.
sign: Return: Laugh if laughter comes; otherwise continue without forcing cheer.

title: The Essence of Laughter
en:
in this three-world joke whose essence is laughter —
to you alone, the non-dual, the one seated in eternal joy:
namas.
brief: Humour and reverence can coexist.
logic: Humour and reverence can coexist. This is an interpretation of a hymn, not evidence that every painful event is deliberately comic
howto: When: When a plan collapses into comedy. Act (suggested modern devotional adaptation): Bow slightly and read the whole prayer rather than perform laughter. Return: Repair what can be repaired, especially if another person is affected.
how: When life turns absurd: say it, and read the absurdity as his seat.
feel: irreverence without disrespect — the sigh turns into a chuckle, and the chuckle lands on him.
sign: Return: Repair what can be repaired, especially if another person is affected.

title: His Laughing-Play
en:
victorious are your servants, lord of the worlds —
for whom this ocean of saṃsāra
is a laughing-play.
brief: The circumstances are not denied: what changes in the poem is the relation of the devotee to the frightening immensity.
logic: The circumstances are not denied: what changes in the poem is the relation of the devotee to the frightening immensity
howto: When: When overwhelmed by the scale of daily trouble. Act (suggested modern devotional adaptation): Read the hymn's ocean image and its description of devotees. Return: Choose one manageable task; amusement is optional.
how: In a hard moment, name it: ocean. Then say the verse, and the water becomes shallow.
feel: the shoulders drop and the mouth lifts before the situation changes at all.
sign: Return: Choose one manageable task; amusement is optional.

title: Angry, Then Laughing, Then Śiva
brief: The verse permits devotion to accompany contradictory emotions.
logic: The verse permits devotion to accompany contradictory emotions. It need not be a manual for escalating or discharging anger
howto: When: When you are furious and want to say something reckless. Act (suggested modern devotional adaptation): Read the full emotional sequence; say Śiva softly at its end if you wish. Return: Do not send the harmful message; act on the issue when you can do so without cruelty.
how: When worked up: say it as an instruction manual — drunk first, then let it become laugh, rise, and shout. The last word must be Śiva, out loud if you dare.
feel: the anger doesn't get suppressed; it gets promoted.
sign: Return: Do not send the harmful message; act on the issue when you can do so without cruelty.

title: The Seed of Sorrow
en:
strange, lord: this mind is by nature the seed of sorrow —
yet watered with the rasa of your devotion
it ripens into the highest fruit.
brief: The poem imagines that a mind carrying sorrow may also carry devotion.
logic: The poem imagines that a mind carrying sorrow may also carry devotion. Grief is not a mistake that must disappear before worship begins
howto: When: When grief makes the mind feel unproductive or ruined. Act (suggested modern devotional adaptation): Read the verse's seed and nourishment image, slowly and without trying to smile. Return: Care for yourself or someone else in one concrete way.
how: In grief: say it and water the seed instead of cursing the soil.
feel: the grief stays, but it is being used; even the tears count as irrigation.
sign: Return: Care for yourself or someone else in one concrete way.

title: The Flood Over Joy and Sorrow
en:
the flood of nectar from meditating you overflows
joy and sorrow alike — like waters filling
all the low and lower lands.
brief: Devotion is represented as a fullness not rationed according to the quality of one's present emotion.
logic: Devotion is represented as a fullness not rationed according to the quality of one's present emotion
howto: When: When comparing how you feel with how you think you ought to feel. Act (suggested modern devotional adaptation): Read the whole flood image. Let gladness or sadness be present without ranking it. Return: Make room for the feeling; if support is needed, ask for it.
how: Say it in either state — grief or glee — the verse works on the level of the field, not the feeling.
feel: a settling, as if water found its level; the ranking of emotions collapses.
sign: Return: Make room for the feeling; if support is needed, ask for it.

title: Sorrow Mixed with Ghee
en:
lord, the countless sorrows even of the world-dweller —
mixed with your own self they become ghee:
they come to be bearable.
brief: The devotional possibility is to include suffering in one's address to Śiva without claiming that suffering becomes pleasant.
logic: The devotional possibility is to include suffering in one's address to Śiva without claiming that suffering becomes pleasant
howto: When: When pain seems too ordinary or ugly to bring into prayer. Act (suggested modern devotional adaptation): Read the source-verified complete verse rather than repeat the current 'ghee' paraphrase. Return: Use appropriate medical, emotional or practical care as needed.
how: In pain: say the ghee line and literally imagine the sharp edge of the feeling being coated.
feel: the body responds to texture, not to reasons — the tightness loosens because the sharpness is now suspended.
sign: Return: Use appropriate medical, emotional or practical care as needed.

title: The Banner Against Suffering
en:
o lord, the banner that destroys the suffering of the bowing —
treasure of good, dhūrjaṭa: for me whose only home is sorrow,
afraid of birth and death — so act for me, that while yet living
i may enjoy the sweet taste of the good sense-objects,
unshakeable, the powers in service of your worship.
brief: An address to the Lord need not wait for a persuasive argument or a purified mood.
logic: An address to the Lord need not wait for a persuasive argument or a purified mood
howto: When: When you cannot compose an eloquent prayer. Act (suggested modern devotional adaptation): Read the complete addressed verse; its vocatives are enough to make a beginning. Return: Rest, talk to someone, or carry out the next necessary step.
how: At 3am in the pit: say the whole confession first, then the name.
feel: the banner is real — a flag planted IN the grief, not flying over it. The fear of birth and death can be said out loud; that's the verse's permission.
sign: Return: Rest, talk to someone, or carry out the next necessary step.

title: The Axe of 'All Is His'
en:
'this is mine, this is not yours' — the roots of attachment and aversion, hard-shackled;
o lord, let the axe of the one conviction 'all is your-become' fall on them in me.
brief: The poem exposes the division enacted by possessiveness; this is contemplation, not an instruction to abandon legitimate boundaries.
logic: The poem exposes the division enacted by possessiveness; this is contemplation, not an instruction to abandon legitimate boundaries
howto: When: When anger is sharpened by possession or comparison. Act (suggested modern devotional adaptation): Read the couplet about mine and yours, naming the actual contested thing to yourself. Return: Keep the boundary if needed, but leave out the contempt.
how: In rage: name the possession first — 'mine', 'not yours' — then say the verse at it.
feel: the fist unclenches not by relaxing but by losing the ownership record; the thing remains, the claiming ends.
sign: Return: Keep the boundary if needed, but leave out the contempt.

title: Let the Anger Ripen
en:
the mind purified by the complete ripening of
honour and dishonour, rāga and the rest —
such a devotee: how could he have ordinary-world conduct?
brief: The devotee can learn to take praise and insult as circumstances, not final definitions of the Self.
logic: The devotee can learn to take praise and insult as circumstances, not final definitions of the Self
howto: When: After praise has inflated you or criticism has burned. Act (suggested modern devotional adaptation): Read the full verse before reacting; see whether honour and dishonour are actually paired. Return: Accept valid feedback; decline the unjust portion; answer without vengeance.
how: When slighted: say it and let the feeling ripen rather than react — the insult is being cooked, not served.
feel: the heat continues but stops being an instruction to act.
sign: Return: Accept valid feedback; decline the unjust portion; answer without vengeance.

title: Devotion Conquers the Darkness
en:
in whose case even the darkness of attachment and aversion
has been conquered by the brilliance of devotion —
what to speak of the learned, among such exalted ones?
brief: The hymn places aversion within a wider account of devotion; it does not excuse harm or require instant forgiveness.
logic: The hymn places aversion within a wider account of devotion; it does not excuse harm or require instant forgiveness
howto: When: When resentment is repeatedly rehearsed. Act (suggested modern devotional adaptation): Read the complete description of devotion and darkness without making the metaphors into physical instructions. Return: Set down the rehearsal for now; make any needed repair or protection.
how: Say it as a light-switch claim: the anger is dark, and you are switching on devotion rather than wrestling the dark.
feel: warmth precedes relief — that order is the physics.
sign: Return: Set down the rehearsal for now; make any needed repair or protection.

title: Your Wrath Purifies
en:
also worthy of praise, O supreme, are those
made pure by the touch of your wrath's fire
even when you have destroyed them.
brief: Devotional literature can address a Lord who is not a sentimental comfort.
logic: Devotional literature can address a Lord who is not a sentimental comfort. Praise can remain demanding and difficult
howto: When: When anger at what has happened includes anger at God. Act (suggested modern devotional adaptation): Read the hymn without changing its harsh words into gentle ones. Return: Be truthful about what happened; seek safety if there is danger.
how: When caught in a rage — yours or someone's's: say it, and re-classify the fire as purifying touch before responding.
feel: the flinch converts to a bow.
sign: Return: Be truthful about what happened; seek safety if there is danger.

title: Victory — the World Depends on Him
en:
victory, lord — namas, namas to you:
this entire universe depends on you;
you are the supreme lord of the worlds, the one —
in you alone i take refuge.
brief: The hymn directs triumph toward Śiva.
logic: The hymn directs triumph toward Śiva. Courage can mean acting without owning the victory
howto: When: Before work that requires courage. Act (suggested modern devotional adaptation): Recite the complete praise and bow once rather than demand confidence. Return: Start the difficult task; let the result remain open.
how: Morning, before the task: say it once under the breath, fast.
feel: the chest widens; effort turns from strain into celebration because the weight is his, not yours.
sign: Return: Start the difficult task; let the result remain open.

title: May I Become the Grass
en:
when, eyes closed in the tasting of inner devotion-wonder,
i worship 'namas to śiva' —
may i become even the grass [in that place].
brief: The heroic gesture here may be relinquishing the need to appear heroic.
logic: The heroic gesture here may be relinquishing the need to appear heroic
howto: When: When effort has become self-display. Act (suggested modern devotional adaptation): Read the full devotional request and, if appropriate, repeat the traditional name Śiva. Return: Do the work that actually needs doing.
how: When enthusiasm needs depth rather than noise: say it and offer to be the least impressive thing in the room.
feel: the wanting-to-be-seen dissolves; the energy continues without the vanity.
sign: Return: Do the work that actually needs doing.

title: The Sound That Never Leaves the Mouth
en:
victorious those on whose mouth's circle
the sound of śiva constantly roams —
ever-streaming from the immortal reservoir,
the supreme nectar dripping sweet.
brief: A small act of remembrance can accompany demanding activity without claiming to control its outcome.
logic: A small act of remembrance can accompany demanding activity without claiming to control its outcome
howto: When: Before public speaking or a difficult action. Act (suggested modern devotional adaptation): Read the source-verified verse about the name moving on devotees' lips. Return: Speak or act as carefully as the occasion requires.
how: Say it when you catch the name rising on its own — mid-shower, mid-walk. The verse applauds the practice applauding itself.
feel: pride WITH devotion; the discipline patting itself on the back.
sign: Return: Speak or act as carefully as the occasion requires.

title: Praised Because You Worship
en:
o mind, though you are flickering, yet you are praised —
because you worship:
you take refuge in the refuge of the refuges,
the teacher of the three worlds, the beloved of ambikā.
brief: Rather than hating an unsettled mind, the devotee recognises the possibility of worship within it.
logic: Rather than hating an unsettled mind, the devotee recognises the possibility of worship within it
howto: When: When attention jumps from task to task. Act (suggested modern devotional adaptation): Read the address to the mind as the poem gives it. Return: Return to one defined action; attention may wander again.
how: Address it TO your mind, in the second person, when it won't hold — praise it for showing up rather than scolding it for drifting.
feel: self-compassion as fuel; the scattered mind sits down when praised, not when punished.
sign: Return: Return to one defined action; attention may wander again.

title: When Will I Suddenly Recognise You
en:
the lord — fearless, generous, full, causeless,
beyond denial of self — when will i suddenly recognise him —
and put the master's own folk to shame?
brief: The text offers refuge in what the devotee takes to be unconditioned.
logic: The text offers refuge in what the devotee takes to be unconditioned. It does not make danger imaginary
howto: When: When the future cannot be guaranteed. Act (suggested modern devotional adaptation): Read the full question or praise about the Lord; keep the grammar of request distinct from declarative certainty. Return: Check actual risks and take proportionate action.
how: When fear is up: say it as a question, not a plea — kadā? when?.
feel: fear becomes the sound before the recognition rather than the enemy of it. After the last word, expect nothing; the asking is the turning.
sign: Return: Check actual risks and take proportionate action.

title: The Full Confession
brief: The devotional address begins with the admitted state, not its elimination.
logic: The devotional address begins with the admitted state, not its elimination
howto: When: When you are afraid and ashamed of being afraid. Act (suggested modern devotional adaptation): Read the confession precisely; do not edit out weakness. Return: Tell someone if help is needed; do not use the prayer instead of safety.
how: List YOUR four in his cadence, then land the last line.
feel: the inventory leaves the body lighter; the refuge-line is the exhale. Especially for aging-anxiety and inadequacy-shame.
sign: Return: Tell someone if help is needed; do not use the prayer instead of safety.

title: The Aghora Mantra
source: Yajurveda · chanted by Swami Lakshmanjoo at every Weekly Sangha
iast: aghorebhyo 'tha ghorebhyo ghoraghoratarībhyaśca | sarvataḥ śarva sarvebhyo namaste rudrarūpebhyaḥ ||
en: salutations to aghora, to ghora, to ghoraghora-tarī — to sarva in all directions, to all the rudra-forms: namas.
brief: The invocation addresses fierce and non-fierce forms alike.
logic: The invocation addresses fierce and non-fierce forms alike. Its devotional move is salutation, not magic protection against all danger
howto: When: When fear makes the mind insist on one monstrous possibility. Act (suggested modern devotional adaptation): Recite the traditional complete formula once if it is part of your practice, slowly and with its repeated salutations. Return: Check your surroundings and do what the situation requires.
how: Chant it where Swamiji put it: at the opening of any practice — this is the beginning of the Weekly Sangha. Three to nine rounds, aloud. When to: first thing in the morning, or at any moment of fear — you are addressing the three energies directly. Effect, per the tradition he taught: protection through the eighteen arms and purification of the three channels, body, speech and mind. His own instruction for its spread: 'You should spread this message all over the world.'
sign: Return: Check your surroundings and do what the situation requires.
feel: FULL MANTRA; do not excerpt an invented bīja

title: The Scorching Dissolved
en:
when will i come to dwell in the drinking-and-playing
of your devotion-nectar — with the eight powers attained,
and all fear of troubles dissolved?
brief: The verse's aspiration can be held without knowing when its desired state will come.
logic: The verse's aspiration can be held without knowing when its desired state will come
howto: When: When fear leads you to bargain for certainty. Act (suggested modern devotional adaptation): Read the whole prayer with its imagery of devotion, not as a guaranteed cure. Return: Return to a safe practical next step.
how: Anxious about what's coming? Take the verse as a drink-description and sip your current state as rasa.
feel: the anticipatory heat cools; the future stops glowing red.
sign: Return: Return to a safe practical next step.

title: The Smear That Is Forgetting
en:
even within, the tiniest smear that is my non-contemplation of you —
wiping that, o lord, from everywhere,
[show] your own form.
brief: The metaphor can open an honest act of repair; it should never amplify hatred of the body or self.
logic: The metaphor can open an honest act of repair; it should never amplify hatred of the body or self
howto: When: When self-disgust makes you want to conceal a mistake. Act (suggested modern devotional adaptation): Read the verse about a stain or lack of remembrance in full. Return: Apologise or correct one thing; then stop rehearsing self-punishment.
how: In self-loathing: rename the stain — it is just the lapse of attention. Wipe = return, not scrub.
feel: the self-hatred loses its subject, and what's left is a fresh look at his form.
sign: Return: Apologise or correct one thing; then stop rehearsing self-punishment.

title: The Impure Mind, Confessed
en:
in my mind, absolutely impure, my own devotion-vine drowned —
hard: it ripens not even its own,
the unearned blossoms of its fortune.
brief: A relationship can be tended after neglect.
logic: A relationship can be tended after neglect. The image is about devotion, not proof that the reader is polluted
howto: When: When devotion feels dry or abandoned. Act (suggested modern devotional adaptation): Read the verse's vine image as lament, not diagnosis. Return: Resume one sustainable practice or ordinary care.
how: Say it on the days you feel worst about yourself — the hymn says it for you, better.
feel: honesty displaces shame; the muck, spoken aloud, is at least seen.
sign: Return: Resume one sustainable practice or ordinary care.

title: The Doubt-Enemy Shattered
en:
the thought-stain in my mind, scoured by the deathless nectar's flood
poured over the trough of refuse — with the invincible doubt-enemy crushed:
let beholding you be unceasing.
brief: Cleansing is a devotional metaphor; moral responsibility remains the appropriate ordinary response.
logic: Cleansing is a devotional metaphor; moral responsibility remains the appropriate ordinary response
howto: When: When regret turns into contempt for yourself. Act (suggested modern devotional adaptation): Read the full praise of cleansing and refuge. Return: Repair a harm where possible; otherwise rest from self-accusation.
how: When the mind feels stained AND doubting: stop scrubbing, start looking — one look inward at the form.
feel: doubt and disgust fall together because they were both standing in the dark.
sign: Return: Repair a harm where possible; otherwise rest from self-accusation.

title: Strike the Dividing-Piece
iast: vilīne śaṅkaughe sapadi paripūrṇe ca vibhave | saṃhārākhyā mama hṛdi bhidāṃśaṃ praharatu
en:
in the melted doubt-heap, at once in full glory —
o lord named dissolution, strike the split portion of my heart.
brief: Its closing petition, if confirmed, addresses inner division without proving that doubt is literally annihilated.
logic: Its closing petition, if confirmed, addresses inner division without proving that doubt is literally annihilated
howto: When: When mental argument keeps recreating an enemy. Act (suggested modern devotional adaptation): Do not recite commercially from the machine-proposed short source; place the verified complete verse after collation. Return: Do not confuse a powerful inward metaphor with permission to strike a person.
how: After weeks of inner division — this vs that, me vs it: say it as the surgeon's request, once.
feel: the split seals; the hunger to divide ends with the knife that isn't yours.
sign: Return: Do not confuse a powerful inward metaphor with permission to strike a person.

title: The Wonder of the Word at Tongue-Tip
en:
when the single word śiva stands ever at the tongue's tip —
the taste of all sense-objects exists in the devotee alone.
what a wonder!
brief: Wonder can coexist with the simplest syllables.
logic: Wonder can coexist with the simplest syllables. The hymn is devotional praise, not a guaranteed transformation of taste
howto: When: When an ordinary sensation suddenly becomes vivid. Act (suggested modern devotional adaptation): Say the name Śiva once and read the verse if available. Return: Return to ordinary sensory attention.
how: When anything tastes or sounds flat: place Śiva at the tongue's tip and re-taste the next sip or bite.
feel: the wonder is measurable — if the flavour deepens, the verse is real.
sign: Return: Return to ordinary sensory attention.

title: The Wonderful Deceiver
en:
namas to the deceptive, the pure, the secret,
the manifest-self, the subtle, the all-form —
to the citra, to śambhu.
brief: Language may point by holding together contrary aspects; the prose gloss should not pretend to solve each paradox.
logic: Language may point by holding together contrary aspects; the prose gloss should not pretend to solve each paradox
howto: When: When something will not fit one description. Act (suggested modern devotional adaptation): Read the verse's deliberately contradictory epithets without flattening them. Return: Let the situation remain complex and respond accurately.
how: When the world turns surreal — say the verse and file the strangeness under citra.
feel: the uncanny flips from threat to artistry; the trick becomes someone's excellent work.
sign: Return: Let the situation remain complex and respond accurately.

title: The Wheel of Diverse States
iast: ya eṣa vitatasphuradvividhabhāvacakrātmakaḥ parasparavibhedavānviṣayatāmupāgacchati yadekamayabhāvanāvaśata etyabhedānvayaṃ sa śaṃbhuraśivāpaho jayati bodhabhāsāṃ nidhiḥ
en: he who, made of the widely flashing wheel of diverse states, comes to be the objects of experience — whose one, given to contemplation, is the bond of non-difference: he, śaṃbhu, averter of woe, triumphs — treasury of the lights of knowing.
brief: The proposed thought is a single luminous reality appearing as difference, not an assertion that differences are fictitious for ordinary purposes.
logic: The proposed thought is a single luminous reality appearing as difference, not an assertion that differences are fictitious for ordinary purposes
howto: When: When the world feels impossibly varied. Act (suggested modern devotional adaptation): Withhold recitation until the edition and the long compound are verified; meanwhile read the draft explanation as editorial commentary. Return: Return attention to one particular thing in the varied world.
how: Use it as the invocation before any prayer-session in this book: name the swirl of your current states as the wheel, then remember the wheel IS the treasury.
feel: the chaos of feelings gets reclassified as treasure on sight.
sign: Return: Return attention to one particular thing in the varied world.

title: Worship Without Begging
en:
wonder! o boon-giver: among the full-hearted in devotion toward you,
is any mode of worship praised
that is not stained with begging?
brief: Astonishment may not need elaborate ritual.
logic: Astonishment may not need elaborate ritual. The poem asks the question rather than prescribing a technique
howto: When: When beauty arrives unexpectedly. Act (suggested modern devotional adaptation): Read the complete questioning verse; do not invent a compulsory gesture. Return: Notice the particular beauty; continue your day.
how: Notice when you've prayed with a shopping list. Say this verse as the correction, then worship once with nothing attached.
feel: the ask drops and the song stays — that gap is the wonder.
sign: Return: Notice the particular beauty; continue your day.

title: The Rasa Beyond the World
en:
diving in the ocean of devotion's nectar — with peaceful waves,
cool and white and sweet — tasting the alaukika rasa:
who among the steady even counts a name there?
brief: The verse praises a devotional fullness in which stillness is welcomed rather than manufactured.
logic: The verse praises a devotional fullness in which stillness is welcomed rather than manufactured
howto: When: When agitation is subsiding. Act (suggested modern devotional adaptation): Read the ocean and nectar imagery without trying to generate an altered state. Return: Rest or work quietly; do not measure progress by calm.
how: For peace-practice: dive once, taste once, count nothing — not even the breath.
feel: the mental to-do list stops being readable; that illegibility is the alaukika flicker.
sign: Return: Rest or work quietly; do not measure progress by calm.

title: All Time in the Worship-Union
brief: The wish is not that ordinary time vanish, but that devotion accompany time as it passes.
logic: The wish is not that ordinary time vanish, but that devotion accompany time as it passes
howto: When: When you wish a peaceful period would last forever. Act (suggested modern devotional adaptation): Read the full wish about time spent in worship. Return: Use the next minute for the duty in front of you.
how: When the day stretches ahead daunting: pray the WHOLE day into the worship-frame, then do the next ordinary thing as its first item.
feel: the horizon softens; time becomes a room, not a corridor.
sign: Return: Use the next minute for the duty in front of you.

title: For Peace, Not for Pleasure
en:
for peace, not for pleasure-seeking — those intoxicated
with the fullness of your devotion, o lord;
even the fruit of searching for liberation they don't crave —
before you, the heart-stealer.
brief: The poem's fullness is not proof that a person should be tranquil under harm.
logic: The poem's fullness is not proof that a person should be tranquil under harm
howto: When: When you are tempted to use spirituality to stop feeling. Act (suggested modern devotional adaptation): Read the complete contrast between devotion and pleasure or quiet. Return: Retain compassion and discernment; take practical action if needed.
how: When peace turns into another acquisition-plan — this retreat, that technique, the next course — say it as the disarming.
feel: the goal releases you; the practice continues unburdened.
sign: Return: Retain compassion and discernment; take practical action if needed.

title: Cries Like Bamboo-Drops
en:
laying my cries at your ear's place, my dearest —
they grow small: like rain inside a bamboo-joint,
they rise as pearls.
brief: Devotion includes speech that is imperfect and fatigued.
logic: Devotion includes speech that is imperfect and fatigued. Silence may follow, but need not be engineered
howto: When: When prayers have become repetitive complaints. Act (suggested modern devotional adaptation): Read the verse's image of addressing the Lord; let its tone remain human. Return: Finish the prayer and move into a small ordinary kindness.
how: When crying or complaining: say it and consciously LAY the noise at his ear — the listener inside.
feel: the sound gets smaller mid-sentence; the bamboo-joint is the quiet place behind your own listening.
sign: Return: Finish the prayer and move into a small ordinary kindness.
